data.long_meaning: Ramila is a combination of two Sanskrit words: Rama, which means 'goddess of love', and Ila, which means 'beauty'. This name is often used to describe the divine feminine embodiment of love, beauty, and protection. The name Ramila carries the meaning “Goddess of love and beauty” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Ramila usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of love and beauty and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: In Indian culture, the name Ramila holds a deep connection with the popular Hindu epic, Ramayana. Ramila refers to the beloved wife of Lord Rama, Sita, who is revered for her unwavering devotion and loyalty to her husband. The name Ramila is thus a reminder of the ideal relationship between a husband and wife, rooted in love, trust, and selflessness.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual standpoint, the name Ramila represents the feminine aspect of the divine, symbolizing compassion, grace, and the nurturing force in the universe. It serves as a reminder of the power of divine love and the importance of cultivating loving relationships in our own lives, leading us towards a deeper connection with the Divine.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ramila was the name of Sita Devi, the consort of Lord Rama in Hindu mythology. The name Ramila carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Ramayana is an ancient Indian epic that narrates the life of Lord Rama and his journey to rescue his wife Sita from the demon king Ravana.

historical_references.reference: Ramila is also the name of a historical queen of the Mauryan Empire in ancient India, who is believed to have ruled around 273 BC – 232 BC.
historical_references.context: The Mauryan Empire was a major power in ancient India and ruled from around 321 BC to 185 BC. Queen Ramila was one of the several queens of Emperor Ashoka.
